**Answer:** The approach uses **only acoustic information** — a Czech-pretrained wav2vec 2.0 base model ("ClTRUS") fine-tuned with `Wav2Vec2ForAudioFrameClassification` on the News-Reading Speech (NRS) corpus of Czech Radio broadcast-news bulletins; it requires **no text annotation and no knowledge of word boundaries** (word-boundary alignment within 100 ms was used for evaluation only), making it audio-modality-only with no handcrafted feature selection. On **within-sentence prosodic boundaries** it reaches **94% accuracy and 83% F1**, rising to **95% accuracy / 89% F1 on all prosodic boundaries**, outperforming a text-based T5 predictor; whole-file frame-level results are Acc 94.87 / F1 88.56 (prosodic boundaries only). Worth noting: the paper's headline is 94%/83% for within-sentence boundaries, while Table 2/3 leave-one-out "all-data" rows print lower numbers (F1 77.40 wav2vec2 vs 82.73 T5 at 0.5 threshold), so the "outperforming the text-based approach" claim is strongest on the abstract-level within-sentence figures.

## (a) What kind of information the approach uses

Verbatim from part 1:

> "In this paper, we apply the wav2vec 2.0 framework to the task of detecting these boundaries in speech signal, **using only acoustic information**. We test the approach on a set of recordings of Czech broadcast news, labeled by phonetic experts, and compare it to an existing text-based predictor, which uses the transcripts of the same data."

> "In this paper, our main goal is to obtain a detector which works **solely in the audio modality, using only acoustic cues**."

> "We have found that the relatively straightforward and easy to use wav2vec 2.0 approach works surprisingly well: **it does not require text annotation or knowledge of word boundaries (these were only used for evaluation)**, nor a handcrafted selection of features, yet it achieves very good results, surpassing the text-based T5 model..."

Key mechanics for (a):

> "We use the pre-trained wav2vec 2.0 base model "ClTRUS"2, which is specifically trained for the Czech language using more than 80 thousand hours of Czech speech from various domains"

> "Using the HuggingFace Transformers library, we fine-tuned the model for an audio frame classification task (Wav2Vec2ForAudioFrameClassification) on the NRS data ... and evaluate it using a leave-one-out approach"

> "The model outputs a label for each audio frame (every 20 ms)."

> "For the purposes of evaluation, these predicted boundaries are then **aligned to the nearest end of a word within 100 ms, based on the reference annotations** – this is because the ground truth phrase boundaries are likewise aligned to the ends of words." (alignment is evaluation-only, not model input)

Data: "recordings of Czech radio broadcast news (Channels 1 and 2 of the Czech Radio) ... the News-Reading Speech (NRS) corpus ... 12 news bulletins presented by different speakers (six male and six female), each between 2.5 and 5 minutes long, for a total of 42 minutes of speech (486 sentences)."

> "the wav2vec2 model achieves an **accuracy of 94% and F1 measure of 83% on within-sentence prosodic boundaries (or 95% and 89% on all prosodic boundaries)**, outperforming the text-based approach."

Related verbatim on the combination models:

> "the listed "T5 OR wav2vec" variants score higher that the individual models alone. However, it is at the cost of slightly reduced precision. Conversely, the "T5 AND wav2vec" achieve a very high precision of ~94 %, but with a relatively low recall of ~60 %."
